cases.name: People-search data should invert into consumer privacy remediation
cases.signal: Large quantities of personal information are aggregated and exposed through people-search and data-broker services.
cases.priorFactoryInterpretation: Public-data source for commercial intelligence and entity resolution.
cases.userInsight: The exposure itself creates consumer pain; identify exposed data, inform the person, and help remove or suppress it using lawful opt-out, deletion, suppression, correction and privacy-right mechanisms.
cases.rootCause: No mandatory pain-inversion or reverse-business operation existed.

painInversion.affectedParty: Consumers whose personal information is publicly aggregated and indexed.
painInversion.pain: Privacy exposure, loss of control over personal contact/location information, and repeated republication across brokers.

remedy.product: Personal Exposure Remediation / Privacy Removal Service
remedy.productLoop: consented exposure scan -> evidence report -> authorized removal/suppression -> verification -> recurring monitoring

candidate.name: Personal Exposure Remediation / Privacy Removal Service
killCriteria: Fewer than 50% of matched commercial-broker exposures are practically removable or suppressible in a controlled pilot.
Median human handling exceeds 20 minutes per paid cleanup after the first 100 cases.
Paid conversion from a consented exposure scan remains below 2% after a statistically useful acquisition test.
